vibe: Never crash, never panic, never copy — build a clean-room InDesign killer with paranoid Rust discipline.
highlights: Crash prevention outranks feature work: no unwrap/expect/panic/unsafe in non-test code, with a last-resort panic guard for command execution and file I/O.
Clean-room legal discipline: InDesign may only be observed black-box via screenshots; never read its bundle, copy assets, or touch GPL/AGPL/LGPL code.
Everything is a command — user-visible behavior must be a command in crates/engine/src/cmd/* with id, label, menu path, shortcut, params, enabled, run, and tests.
Layering enforced by cargo xtask layers; nothing below L6 may depend on egui/eframe/winit/rfd, keeping the UI crate swappable.
Quality gates before every commit: cargo xtask ci (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm) with one task id per commit.
assessment: This file treats crash-safety as a first-class architectural constraint rather than a code-review afterthought, which is exactly right for a document editor where a panic means lost user work. The clean-room rules are unusually precise about what may and may not be observed or copied, showing mature legal and ethical awareness rare in agent instructions. The command-centric design and enforced layering give agents a single, testable seam for all behavior, making autonomous operation tractable without sacrificing rigor.
